Is Your Panel the Bottleneck? Electrical Service Upgrades in Kennewick

There's a collision happening in Kennewick's older neighborhoods. The houses — solid mid-century ranches from the Hanford boom years — were wired for a 1960 idea of electricity: 100 amps, sometimes 60, feeding a range, a water heater, and some lights. The lives inside them are 2020s electric lives: heat pumps replacing old furnaces, EVs in the driveway, hot tubs, shop tools, two refrigerators. The panel is where those two eras meet, and increasingly it's where the older era loses.

Beyond raw capacity, some panels are problems in themselves. Certain brands common in this region's mid-century construction — Zinsco and Federal Pacific among them — have documented failure modes where breakers don't trip under fault, and many insurers and home inspectors now flag them on sight. If your panel wears one of those names, the upgrade conversation isn't about amps at all; it's about a device that may not do its one safety job.

A panel or service upgrade is permitted, inspected, utility-coordinated work. We can connect you with licensed electrical contractors in the Tri-Cities who handle the whole sequence, including the utility disconnect and reconnect.

Common electrical panel upgrades situations in Kennewick

A full panel with nowhere to land new circuits

The practical trigger for most upgrades: you want a heat pump, EV charger, or shop subpanel and there are no open slots — and the tandem-breaker tricks are exhausted. A 200-amp panel with generous spaces solves the next twenty years of additions at once.

Zinsco, Federal Pacific, and other flagged panels

These brands turn up regularly in Kennewick homes of the 1955–1980 window. The issue isn't age but design: documented cases of breakers failing to trip during faults. Insurance carriers increasingly surcharge or decline homes carrying them, which makes replacement part safety, part financial housekeeping.

Warm panels, buzzing breakers, flickering under load

Heat and sound at the panel mean resistance at connections — the precursor to arcing. In heavy-electric-use Tri-Cities households these symptoms deserve prompt professional eyes, whatever the panel's brand or age.

How it works

  1. 1

    Load calculation and panel assessment

    An electrician runs the numbers on your current and planned loads (NEC load calc), inspects the existing panel and service entrance, and tells you whether you need a bigger service or just a better panel at the same amperage.

  2. 2

    Permits and utility coordination

    Panel and service work requires an L&I electrical permit, and a service upgrade means scheduling the local utility for disconnect and reconnect. Your contractor handles both; the utility step is what sets the project date.

  3. 3

    The swap — usually one day

    Power goes off in the morning; the new panel, grounding updates, and any service-entrance work happen during the day; power returns by evening. Every circuit gets landed, tested, and labeled — an incidental gift to whoever troubleshoots the house next.

  4. 4

    State inspection

    An L&I inspector reviews and signs off the work. Keep the paperwork with your house documents; it answers the question every future buyer's inspector will ask.

What electrical panel upgrades costs in Kennewick

In the Tri-Cities, a like-amperage panel replacement (swapping a problem panel at existing 100–125A service) is the smaller project; a full 200-amp service upgrade — new panel, meter base, service entrance conductors, grounding, utility coordination — is the larger, typically low-to-mid four figures depending on how much of the service entrance needs rebuilding. Masted overhead services common in older Kennewick neighborhoods sometimes need mast and weatherhead work that adds scope. If an EV charger or heat pump is the trigger, price the panel and the new circuit together — combined trips cost less than sequential ones.

Frequently asked questions

How do I know if my house has a Zinsco or Federal Pacific panel?

Open the panel door (just the door) and read the label — Zinsco, Sylvania-Zinsco, or Federal Pacific 'Stab-Lok' are the flag names. Zinsco breakers often have distinctive colored handles. If you see one, an electrician's assessment is worth scheduling even without symptoms.

Is 100 amps enough for a Kennewick home?

For a gas-heated home with modest loads, often yes. For the local norm — electric heat or heat pump, electric water heater, electric range, plus AC — 100 amps is already snug, and adding an EV charger usually tips it. The load calculation, not the square footage, gives the real answer.

How long is the power out during a panel upgrade?

Typically one working day — off in the morning, on by evening. Cold-season swaps are gentler on the household here than August ones, when a day without AC in 100°F heat is its own event. Plan the fridge and freezer accordingly either way.

Will my insurance really care about my old panel?

Increasingly yes. Many carriers now ask panel brand at quote time, and some decline or surcharge homes with Federal Pacific or Zinsco equipment. Replacing one can directly lower premiums — ask your agent for numbers before and after; it sometimes materially changes the payback math.

Can I upgrade the panel myself in Washington?

Washington allows homeowners to do electrical work on their own primary residence with a homeowner permit and inspection — but service work involves the utility, load-side and line-side hazards, and grounding details that fail inspections. This is one of the trades where even committed DIYers usually hire out.
